title: Renew or upgrade a NSW driver licence
summary: You can renew or upgrade your NSW Driver Licence online if you meet specific eligibility criteria.
intro:
If you meet certain eligibility criteria, you can renew or upgrade your NSW Driver Licence online.

The term that you renew or upgrade for depends on the licence class:

Note: You'll need to visit a Service NSW Centre in person if you'd like a 10-year licence (available for drivers aged 21 to 44) or if any of the reasons you may not be able to renew or upgrade online apply to you.
who_can_apply: You must meet the eyesight requirements.
You must hold an eligible driver licence that expires in 6 months or less, or one that expired no more than 6 months ago.
You must be aged 17 years or over (up to 70 if your licence class is MC).
Your up-to-date medical conditions must be recorded with Transport for NSW (TfNSW), and your NSW Fitness to Drive medical assessment must not be overdue.
Your licence must not be subject to any restrictions related to enforcement (e.g., cancelled, disqualified, suspended, refused, or pending an appeal or suspension decision).
You must have had your signature and photograph taken by TfNSW within 10.5 years before the new licence expires.
Your licence must have an interlock or Q (temporary overseas visitor) condition.
If upgrading from P1 to P2, you must have held your P1 licence for at least 12 months (excluding any suspension period).
If upgrading from P2 to full, you must have held your P2 licence for at least 2 years (excluding any suspension period).
If you hold a dual class licence where one class is full C or R and the other is P1 or P2, you may renew the full class and upgrade the provisional class at the same time.

If you are 25 years or over and hold a dual class licence where one class is full C, LR, MR, HR, HC, or MC and the other class is R P1 (held for at least 12 months) or R P2, and you are renewing the full class, the R P1 or P2 will automatically upgrade to full.
what_you_need: The licence fee, or your concession details.
If renewing or upgrading in person, you should find out what is needed at a Service NSW Centre.

how_to_steps.text: Select the 'Renew or upgrade licence' button.
Log in, or create your MyServiceNSW Account. Enter your NSW driver licence details if your account is new or you haven't previously entered them.
Follow the prompts to renew or upgrade your driver licence.
Download or update your Digital Driver Licence on the Service NSW app or print your interim paper licence.
Your new NSW driver licence card will be posted to you at the mailing address on record with TfNSW. You should receive it within 15 business days.

more_info.text: If you renew online, your new licence card will be printed using the photo already stored by TfNSW.
Carry your old licence card with you when you drive, if you still have it.
If your temporary paper licence is lost, stolen or damaged before you receive your new licence card, you can get a copy of it online.
If you have not received your card within 15 business days, please call us on 13 77 88.

At a service centre, you're able to apply for a NSW Photo Card at the same time if you wish, and take advantage of paying a reduced application fee for it. The NSW Photo Card is voluntary – you don't have to have one, but you may find it useful to prove your identity in situations not related to driving.
Your new expiry date(s) will be displayed onscreen when you’re renewing online. Depending on the term you chose, your expiry date(s) will differ.
If you got your P1 Car licence before 20 November 2017, you'll need to pass the Hazard Perception Test (HPT).
If you upgrade from P1 to P2 online, you must make sure you have the correct P plates to display while you're driving.

faqs.q: Do I need to visit a Service NSW Centre in person?
faqs.a: You must visit a Service NSW Centre in person if you want a 10-year licence (for drivers aged 21 to 44) or if any of the reasons listed prevent you from renewing or upgrading online.

faqs.q: What are the eyesight requirements for renewal?
faqs.a: If you are less than 45 years old, you must have passed an eyesight test within 10.5 years of the new licence expiring. If you are 45 years or older, you must have passed an eyesight test within 5.5 years of the new licence expiring.

faqs.q: What happens if I have a dual class licence?
faqs.a: If you are 25 years or over and hold a dual class licence where one class is full C, LR, MR, HR, HC, or MC, and the other class is R P1 (held for at least 12 months) or R P2, the provisional class will automatically upgrade to full when you renew the full class.
